ledger.note: Early 13th century BC: Muwatalli II makes Tarhuntassa the Hittite capital. 'Muwatalli II moved the Hittite capital from Hattusa to Tarhuntassa' (page: early 13th century BC, reasons unclear). The page dates nothing more exactly; -1280 is a bridge inside the century, and the city's location is unknown.

ledger.note: 13th century BC (bridged): Hattusili III makes Tarhuntassa a vassal kingdom. Mursili III moved the capital back to Hattusa, Hattusili III deposed him and 'appointed Muwatalli's son Kurunta as king in Tarhuntassa' (treaty usually naming him Ulmi-Tessup); Tudhaliya IV later re-ratified Kurunta on the Bronze Tablet. The page dates none of it; -1267 sits between the hittites dossier's Kadesh year (1274) and its Egyptian treaty year (1258).

sources.title: Tarhuntassa
sources.note: Capital moved by Muwatalli II in the early 13th century, Mursili III, Hattusili III's appointment of Kurunta, Tudhaliya IV's Bronze Tablet, Suppiluliuma II's sack; the site is unknown; no infobox, no area, no dates beyond the century.

notes: Cliopatria has no Tarhuntassa. The page is almost wholly undated (early 13th century for the capital move, Late Bronze Age occupation c. 1300-1100 at one candidate site), so every event is a confidence-1 bridge and the shape is a placeholder from the proposed sites. The page says Tarhuntassa 'may have been another name for the Hulaya River Land' (Bryce 1974), which would put it on the Arzawa side of the Hittite settlement; this reading is not used. The Seha River Land and Mira appear only as treaty witnesses and are not placed. The hittites dossier (me-04-a) does not mention Tarhuntassa, so its capital move (Hattusa to Tarhuntassa and back) has no counterpart there. Page budget: one page.
